**To:**
Shri Ramesh Chandra Agrawal
S/o Late Shri Kailash Narayan Agrawal
E-7/44, Arera Colony, Bhopal (M.P.) 462016

**From:**
Ms. Anjali Verma
D/o Shri Suresh Verma
[TO CONFIRM]
Bhopal (M.P.)

**Date:** 20 September 2026

**Subject: Counter-Notice — Objections to Rent Agreement dated 1 April 2026 for Flat No. 302, Shanti Residency, Kolar Road, Bhopal — Without Prejudice — For Review by Supervising Advocate Before Service**

---

Dear Shri Agrawal,

I, Ms. Anjali Verma, Lessee in respect of Flat No. 302, Second Floor, Shanti Residency, Kolar Road, Bhopal, hereby place on record my formal objections to several clauses of the Rent Agreement executed between us on **1 April 2026** ("the Agreement"). This notice is issued without prejudice to all my rights and remedies in law and equity, and is prepared for the review of my supervising advocate before service.

**Prior Correspondence:** [TO CONFIRM] — whether Ms. Anjali Verma has previously sent any written demand or response to the Lessor prior to this notice, or whether this is the first written communication from the Lessee.

The objections are set out clause-by-clause below:

---

**Objection 1 — Clause 1 (Term): Compulsory Registration Not Complied With**

Clause 1 of the Agreement contemplates occupation of the Premises for up to **thirty-six months** through automatic renewals. A lease of immovable property for a term exceeding one year must be **compulsorily registered** under the applicable registration law (Rule REG-17). The Agreement has been executed on stamp paper of Rs. 100 only (Clause 12) and has not been registered. An unregistered instrument required to be registered cannot be received in evidence of any transaction affecting the property or conferring the terms of the lease (Rule REG-49). Accordingly, I put you on notice that any attempt to enforce the penal, restrictive or asymmetric provisions of the unregistered Agreement against me will be resisted on this ground.

I call upon you to either:
(a) execute a properly stamped and registered agreement reflecting mutually agreed and lawful terms; or
(b) acknowledge in writing that the Agreement shall not be enforced beyond the initial 11-month term without fresh registration.

---

**Objection 2 — Clause 4 (Security Deposit): Excess Deposit and Unlawful Forfeiture Clause**

The security deposit collected amounts to Rs. 3,00,000, equivalent to six months' rent. For residential premises, the applicable law caps the security deposit at **two months' rent** (Rule MTA-11). The permissible cap on this basis would be [TO CONFIRM], and the excess collected would accordingly be [TO CONFIRM] — these figures are to be verified by the supervising advocate before finalisation.

Further, the clause permits the Lessor to deduct "such sums as the Lessor may in his sole discretion determine." A clause enabling forfeiture of the security deposit without accounting for actual dues or damage is unenforceable beyond genuine and demonstrated loss (Rule FORFEITURE).

I demand:
(a) refund of the excess deposit (being the amount over the statutory cap, quantum [TO CONFIRM]) within **15 days** of this notice; and
(b) your written confirmation that any deduction from the deposit at the time of vacation will be supported by an itemised account of actual damage or dues.

---

**Objection 3 — Clause 5 (Lock-In): Asymmetric and Unenforceable**

Clause 5 imposes a 24-month lock-in exclusively on the Lessee while expressly exempting the Lessor from any corresponding restriction. A one-sided lock-in is enforceable only to the extent of the Lessor's actual demonstrable loss on early vacation — it cannot operate as an absolute prohibition (Rule LOCKIN). The asymmetric nature of the clause also renders it opposed to public policy and void to that extent (Rule CA-23).

I put you on notice that if I am required to vacate before the lock-in period, I shall be liable only for such **actual, proved loss** as you can demonstrate, and not for any automatic penalty.

---

**Objection 4 — Clause 6 (Penalty): Penalty Plus Full Forfeiture Without Proof of Loss**

Clause 6 provides for payment of Rs. 50,000 as penalty **in addition** to forfeiture of the **entire** security deposit of Rs. 3,00,000, expressly "whether or not the Lessor proves any loss." Under the applicable law on penalty clauses, recovery is limited to **reasonable compensation not exceeding the named sum** — the phrase "whether or not the Lessor proves any loss" does not expand this entitlement, and cumulative double recovery through both a named penalty and blanket deposit forfeiture is not permitted (Rule CA-74). The phrase "whether or not the Lessor proves any loss" is void and of no effect.

I shall resist any claim under Clause 6 that exceeds reasonable compensation as determined by law.

---

**Objection 5 — Clause 7 (Utilities): Threatened Disconnection of Essential Services**

Clause 7 purports to entitle the Lessor to disconnect electricity and water supply without notice if rent is unpaid for fifteen days. A landlord cannot cut off or withhold water, electricity or other essential supply to the premises, even during a dispute, except in accordance with law (Rule ESSENTIAL-SERVICES). Any such disconnection will expose you to legal liability.

I reserve my right to seek appropriate legal remedy, including injunctive relief, should any disconnection be attempted.

---

**Objection 6 — Clause 8 (Notice): Asymmetric and Below Statutory Minimum**

Clause 8 allows the Lessor to terminate on a mere **seven days'** notice while requiring the Lessee to give **three months'** notice. The applicable law requires the landlord to give at least **one month's notice** before evicting a residential tenant (Rule MTA-NOTICE). Seven days' notice is below the statutory minimum and is unenforceable. The asymmetry in the notice period is also contrary to public policy (Rule CA-23).

I shall treat any purported termination on seven days' notice as invalid in law.

---

**Objection 7 — Clause 9 (Entry): Entry Without Notice Violates Quiet Enjoyment**

Clause 9 entitles the Lessor or his agents to enter the Premises "at any hour for inspection, without prior intimation." The law requires at least **24 hours' prior notice** before entry for inspection or repairs, except in genuine emergencies (Rule ARBITRARY-ENTRY). Entry without notice also violates the Lessee's right to quiet enjoyment, which is a statutory duty of the Lessor (Rule TPA-108).

I require you to give me at least 24 hours' written notice before any entry, and I shall refuse entry in breach of this requirement.

---

**Objection 8 — Clause 11 (Repairs): Unlawful Transfer of Structural Repair Obligations**

Clause 11 purports to transfer **all repairs, whether structural or otherwise**, to the Lessee at her own cost. The Lessor's statutory duty of disclosure of material defects and the Lessee's right to carry out necessary repairs neglected by the Lessor and deduct their reasonable cost from rent cannot be completely excluded by agreement (Rule TPA-108). A blanket exclusion of the Lessor's liability for all structural repairs is unenforceable.

I shall not accept liability for structural repairs that are the Lessor's responsibility in law.

---

**Objection 9 — Clause 3 (Escalation): Automatic Increase Not Tied to Permitted Statutory Grounds**

Clause 3 provides for an automatic rent increase of 12% on completion of every eleven months. Under the applicable law (Rule MPACA-RENT-INC), rent may be increased only on specific permitted grounds — such as improvements made to the premises or a rise in applicable taxes or charges — and not arbitrarily or by a fixed contractual percentage unconnected to those grounds. The automatic 12% escalation in Clause 3 is not expressly linked to any such permitted ground and may therefore be unenforceable to that extent. I reserve the right to challenge any escalation that is not justified by improvements or a rise in taxes before the Rent Controlling Authority.

---

**Demands and Timeline**

In light of the foregoing, I call upon you to:
1. Respond to this notice within **15 days** of its receipt, i.e., by **[TO CONFIRM]**;
2. Refund the excess security deposit (quantum [TO CONFIRM]) within 15 days of this notice;
3. Execute a fresh, properly stamped and registered tenancy agreement on lawful terms if you wish the tenancy to continue beyond the initial 11-month term;
4. Provide written assurance that essential services will not be disconnected;
5. Confirm that entry will henceforth be on at least 24 hours' prior written notice.

---

**Reservation of Rights**

All rights, remedies and contentions available to me in law and equity are expressly reserved. Nothing in this notice shall be construed as an admission of liability or as a waiver of any right. This notice is issued without prejudice to any proceedings that may be initiated before the appropriate court, tribunal or Rent Controlling Authority.

Yours faithfully,

________________________
**Ms. Anjali Verma**
Lessee, Flat No. 302, Shanti Residency, Kolar Road, Bhopal
Date: 20 September 2026
Place: Bhopal

*[This draft is prepared for review and approval by the supervising advocate and is NOT to be served in this form without such review.]*
